title: Convergence and Diagnostics
text: vignette shows simple workflow checking whether sampler appears stable practice. package now supports multiple chains, including R-level parallel execution, examples combine: traceplots, running means, effective sample size approximations, repeated fits different seeds.

title: Convergence and Diagnostics
code: library(exnexSurv) library(survival) library(ggplot2) library(bayesplot)  simulate_surv_data <- function(   theta,   sigma2,   beta = NULL,   n_per_group = 60,   censor_min = 4,   censor_max = 12,   seed = NULL ) {   if (!is.null(seed)) {     set.seed(seed)   }    groups <- rep(seq_along(theta), each = n_per_group)   age_std <- rnorm(length(groups), mean = 0, sd = 1)   mean_log_time <- rep(theta, each = n_per_group)    if (!is.null(beta)) {     mean_log_time <- mean_log_time + beta * age_std   }    log_time <- rnorm(length(groups), mean = mean_log_time, sd = sqrt(sigma2))   true_time <- exp(log_time)   censor_time <- runif(length(groups), min = censor_min, max = censor_max)    data.frame(     time = pmin(true_time, censor_time),     event = as.integer(true_time <= censor_time),     group = factor(groups),     age_std = age_std   ) }  sim_data <- simulate_surv_data(   theta = c(1.2, 1.7, 2.1),   sigma2 = 0.20,   beta = -0.35,   n_per_group = 60,   seed = 6841 )  mean(sim_data$event) #> [1] 0.6777778

code: running_mean_df <- do.call(   rbind,   lapply(colnames(fit$draws), function(param) {     values <- fit$draws[[param]]     data.frame(       iteration = seq_along(values),       running_mean = cumsum(values) / seq_along(values),       parameter = param     )   }) )  ggplot(running_mean_df, aes(iteration, running_mean)) +   geom_line() +   facet_wrap(~ parameter, scales = "free_y") +   labs(     title = "Running posterior means",     x = "Post-warmup iteration",     y = "Running mean"   )

title: Convergence and Diagnostics
text: Lower autocorrelation higher effective sample size usually preferable.
code: ess_simple <- function(x, max_lag = 100) {   acf_vals <- stats::acf(     x,     lag.max = min(max_lag, length(x) - 1),     plot = FALSE   )$acf[-1]    positive_acf <- acf_vals[acf_vals > 0]    if (length(positive_acf) == 0) {     return(length(x))   }    tau <- 1 + 2 * sum(positive_acf)   min(length(x), length(x) / tau) }  diagnostics <- data.frame(   parameter = colnames(fit$draws),   mean = colMeans(fit$draws),   sd = apply(fit$draws, 2, sd),   lag1_acf = apply(fit$draws, 2, function(x) stats::acf(x, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE)$acf[2]),   ess = apply(fit$draws, 2, ess_simple),   mcse = mapply(function(s, e) s / sqrt(e), apply(fit$draws, 2, sd), apply(fit$draws, 2, ess_simple)),   row.names = NULL )  diagnostics #>   parameter       mean         sd   lag1_acf      ess         mcse #> 1   theta_1  1.2463566 0.06462694 0.07715308 1670.518 0.0015812045 #> 2   theta_2  1.7120960 0.06780666 0.17671633 1401.528 0.0018112211 #> 3   theta_3  2.1643972 0.07989574 0.36812889 1153.227 0.0023526984 #> 4    beta_1 -0.3834375 0.04700082 0.33138567 1187.507 0.0013639152 #> 5    sigma2  0.2321148 0.03015053 0.33885848 1020.186 0.0009439638

title: The EXNEX Model, Priors, and Data Augmentation
text: Basket trials enroll patients several small groups (baskets), often defined biomarker, tumor histology, cancer type, studied common protocol. basket typically contains handful patients, separately estimating effect every basket imprecise, pooling patients single estimate ignores real differences baskets. Borrowing information across baskets strikes middle ground: baskets look alike share strength, baskets disagree majority allowed stand apart. EXNEX (Exchangeable–Non-Exchangeable) framework extends standard exchangeable hierarchical model attaching latent indicator every basket selects whether effect drawn shared exchangeable component basket-specific non-exchangeable prior [@neuenschwander2016]. exnexSurv implements EXNEX right-censored, log-normal survival data using data-augmented Gibbs sampler written C++ via Rcpp RcppArmadillo [@eddelbuettel2011rcpp; @sanderson2016armadillo]. vignette explains model, priors customize , data augmentation mechanism makes sampler exact fast, systematic Gibbs scan, fitted object contains. short worked example illustrates shrinkage prior customization. statistical methodology described detail companion paper (Ney, 2026); performance numbers quoted last section taken .

code: fit <- exnex_surv(   Surv(time, event) ~ group,   data = d,   priors = list(     p_mix  = 0.7,     v_nex  = 10,     a_tau  = 3,     b_tau  = 3,     v_beta = 10   ) ) library(exnexSurv) library(survival) library(ggplot2)  simulate_basket_data <- function(   theta,   sigma = 1.2,   beta = c(0.8, -0.5),   group_sizes = c(30, 24, 20, 16, 14, 11, 8, 7, 5),   target_cens = 0.30,   seed = 1 ) {   set.seed(seed)   K <- length(theta)   group <- rep(seq_len(K), times = group_sizes)   n <- length(group)   X1 <- rnorm(n)   X2 <- rnorm(n)   eta <- theta[group] + X1 * beta[1] + X2 * beta[2]   log_time <- eta + rnorm(n, 0, sigma)   true_time <- exp(log_time)   censor_fun <- function(c) mean(true_time > c) - target_cens   censor_time <- uniroot(censor_fun, c(min(true_time), max(true_time)))$root   data.frame(     time = pmin(true_time, censor_time),     event = as.integer(true_time <= censor_time),     group = factor(group),     X1 = X1,     X2 = X2   ) }  theta_true <- c(1.5, 1.4, 1.6, 1.45, 1.55, 1.5, -0.4, -0.6, -0.5) d <- simulate_basket_data(theta_true, seed = 1)  # small, quick fit just to inspect resolved_priors quick <- exnex_surv(   Surv(time, event) ~ group + X1 + X2,   data = d,   priors = list(p_mix = 0.7, v_nex = 10),   iter = 400, warmup = 200, chains = 1 ) print(quick$resolved_priors) #> $a_sigma #> [1] 2 #>  #> $b_sigma #> [1] 2 #>  #> $a_tau #> [1] 2 #>  #> $b_tau #> [1] 2 #>  #> $p_mix #> [1] 0.7 #>  #> $m_mu #> [1] 0 #>  #> $v_mu #> [1] 10000 #>  #> $m_nex #> [1] 0 #>  #> $v_nex #> [1] 10 #>  #> $v_beta #> [1] 10000

title: The EXNEX Model, Priors, and Data Augmentation
text: companion paper data-augmented Gibbs sampler compared marginalized Stan NUTS implementation EXNEX model 12,000 simulated trials (plus 1,000 TCGA-calibrated). four primary scenarios two implementations produced essentially identical posterior summaries, Gibbs averaged roughly 0.70–0.74 seconds per trial versus 16.96–17.53 seconds Stan (median runtime ratio 25×\times), delivered roughly ten times bulk effective samples per second (3,854–4,032 versus 338–391). Operating characteristics (bias, RMSE, interval coverage) EXNEX close nominal across scenarios , Mixed efficacy, EXNEX clearly outperformed Complete pooling (failed resistant baskets) pooling (inefficient responsive baskets). figures hardware- implementation-dependent; quoted convey order magnitude speedup data augmentation makes possible.

title: Running Chains in Parallel
text: exnexSurv can run multiple independent MCMC chains , requested, distribute across R-level parallel workers. C++ sampler still handles one chain per call; R bridge coordinates chain loop combines post-warmup draws. Use: chains total number independent chains, parallel_chains many chains run concurrently. parallel_chains must less equal chains.

title: Running Chains in Parallel
code: library(exnexSurv) library(survival)  simulate_surv_data <- function(   theta,   sigma2,   beta = NULL,   n_per_group = 40,   censor_min = 4,   censor_max = 12,   seed = NULL ) {   if (!is.null(seed)) {     set.seed(seed)   }    groups <- rep(seq_along(theta), each = n_per_group)   age_std <- rnorm(length(groups))   mean_log_time <- rep(theta, each = n_per_group)    if (!is.null(beta)) {     mean_log_time <- mean_log_time + beta * age_std   }    log_time <- rnorm(length(groups), mean = mean_log_time, sd = sqrt(sigma2))   true_time <- exp(log_time)   censor_time <- runif(length(groups), min = censor_min, max = censor_max)    data.frame(     time = pmin(true_time, censor_time),     event = as.integer(true_time <= censor_time),     group = factor(groups),     age_std = age_std   ) }  sim_data <- simulate_surv_data(   theta = c(1.0, 1.6, 2.1),   sigma2 = 0.25,   beta = -0.30,   seed = 9201 )

title: Fit Bayesian EXNEX Survival Models — exnex_surv
text: patient \(\), model $$\log T_i = \theta_{g[]} + X_i^{\mathsf T}\beta + \varepsilon_i,\quad \varepsilon_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2),$$ latent EXNEX hierarchy basket effects, $$\theta_j\mid Z_j\sim Z_j\,\mathcal N(\mu,\tau^2) +(1-Z_j)\,\mathcal N(m_{0j},v_{0j}),\quad Z_j\sim\mathrm{Bern}(p_{\mathrm{exch},j}),$$ basket either borrows strength exchangeable component \(\mathcal N(\mu,\tau^2)\) follows non-exchangeable prior \(\mathcal N(m_{0j},v_{0j})\). first predictor variable model formula interpreted basket/group assignment; additional variables covariates linear predictor log-survival scale. Censored event times handled data augmentation: censored log-time imputed truncated-Normal conditional distribution (inverse-CDF log space) remaining parameters updated conjugate full conditionals. sampler keeps posterior draws \(\theta_j\), \(\beta\), \(\sigma^2\).
